changes.before: Change items[1] to items[[1]]. What type prints?
changes.after: A list can hold values of different types. Single brackets can return a smaller list.

before: list(score=7, topic="stars") stores a number and text as separate components without forcing one common atomic type.
items[1] returns a one-component list. items[[1]] extracts the component itself. That extracted component can be a vector or another complex object.

items$score is convenient for a fixed component name. For programmatically supplied exact names, [[ with an explicit name is clearer than relying on partial matching.

[[ with index 1 and $ with fixed name score both extract the stored component itself here, not a one-component list. Each returns the numeric value 7.
```r
items <- list(score = 7, topic = "stars")
cat(items[[1]], items$score, sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
7,7
```

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
items <- list(score=7, topic="stars")
cat(typeof(items[1]))
```
